why: The student treats t = a as linking t to a, so t seems to follow a when a changes. From that wrong rule they conclude both variables end up as b. In fact t keeps a's old value, so b gets the old a and the two values are exchanged.

concepts.quote: Then b = t means b equals a, so both are b.
concepts.why: They miss that t saved a's old value, so they don't see the exchange and wrongly decide both variables hold b.

concepts.quote: b = t means b equals a
concepts.why: They treat t as holding 'a' itself rather than the value a had when t = a ran, so t seems to change when a changes.
The code has no arrays, and the answer says nothing about array references.
